key_insight: Machine learning models using only routine EHR demographics could modestly help identify patients likely to have unmet health-related social needs (HRSNs).
clinical_relevance: This could support targeted outreach and screening efforts in primary care and community health settings, but it is not accurate enough to replace direct HRSN screening.
method: Trained logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM models on EHR data
Used non-modifiable sociodemographic features available in routine records
Compared models with 10-fold cross-validation for overall and individual HRSN prediction
evidence_signal: In 745,975 patients from OCHIN community health centers (2016-2022), LightGBM achieved the best overall AUROC at 64.5%, with similar modest performance across individual HRSN outcomes.
watch_item: Performance was only modest, and relying on demographic features alone may limit fairness, precision, and real-world usefulness without added clinical or area-level context.
paper_title: Leveraging Machine Learning Approaches to Identify Health-Related Social Needs Screening from Electronic Health Records
